subject: Re: Dedicated GPU commits — capacity unit definition & SLA redlines
messages:
From: Elena Santos <elena.santos@healthgrid.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai, procurement@healthgrid.com
Cc: Daniel Kim <daniel.kim@healthgrid.com>
Date: Wed, 8 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated GPU commitment — clarifying capacity unit definition

Jonas / Redwood team,

Thanks for the call this morning. We're interested in the Dedicated offering but need clarity on a couple of contract items before procurement can move forward with the SOW. Attaching the redlines the legal team asked us to capture (HealthGrid_Redlines_v1.docx). Key open questions: 

1) Definition of "Capacity Unit" — your sales doc refers to units but doesn't say how those map to GPU types, vram, or expected throughput (tokens/sec or requests/sec). We need an explicit definition to size our pools and to justify the commit to Finance.

2) Throughput guarantees — the draft SLA references "throughput targets" measured at the cluster level. We need per-tenant guarantees (or a clear measurement methodology) and a perf metric (p95 latency or tokens/sec) that we can audit during the term.

3) Service credit caps — our legal prefers credit caps at 25% of the monthly Dedicated fee for severe outages; your earlier email referenced 10% which our CFO thinks is low given our reliance. Please confirm your standard position.

4) Burst capacity — how much burst is included vs billed overage? We have predictable spikes during batch runs and need to know how that will be handled.

Can we get a proposed clean definition you would accept for "Capacity Unit" and a short note on measurement methodology? Once we have that, Procurement and Legal can finalize the SOW sign-off.

Thanks,
Elena Santos
Director of Infrastructure Procurement
HealthGrid

---
Attachment: HealthGrid_Redlines_v1.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document, 46KB)

From: jonas.weber@redwood.ai <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Santos <elena.santos@healthgrid.com>
Cc: karchik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, procurement@healthgrid.com
Date: Wed, 8 Jul 2026 12:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU commitment — clarifying capacity unit definition

Elena — thanks for the clear summary and the redlines doc. I pulled in Karthik (pricing) and Marissa (legal) to make sure we address everything. High level answers below and a proposed definition attached.

Short answers (details below):
- Capacity Unit (DCU): 1 DCU = baseline capacity equivalent to a single A100-80GB physical GPU operating at 70% sustained high-utilization profile for inference workloads measured over a 5-minute rolling window. We map other GPU types to DCUs via a perf-normalization table (attached) so commits are hardware-agnostic.
- Throughput measurement: we propose measuring per-tenant guaranteed throughput as sustained tokens/sec averaged over 5-minute windows, reported by Redwood Console. Audit logs and metrics are available for both parties.
- Service credit cap: Our standard cap is 15% of Monthly Dedicated fees. We can go to 20% for a 24+ month commit or at a higher commit tier.
- Burst allowance: Each DCU includes a 20% burst headroom for short spikes (max 15 minutes in any 1-hour window). Excess burst beyond that is billed as overage at the committed unit rate * 1.5.

Attached: Dedicated_Pricing_Proposal_jonas_v2.pdf (proposal with mapping table, tiered discounts, and SLA wording).

Detailed proposal (for your procurement/legal teams):
1) Capacity unit definition (proposed language to include in SOW):
   "Dedicated Capacity Unit (DCU): A contractually defined unit of baseline Dedicated capacity. One DCU equals the performance baseline of an NVIDIA A100-80GB GPU executing inference workloads and achieving X tokens/sec at 70% sustained utilization. Redwood will publish a GPU-to-DCU mapping table in the SOW to translate physical GPU types provided under the Dedicated environment into DCUs. Redwood reserves the right to select GPU hardware subject to the mapping table but will not change the mapping without 90 days' notice and an agreed test run.
   Measurement: Throughput and utilization are measured by the Redwood Console metrics for the Tenant ID identified in the SOW, using 5-minute rolling windows and 1-minute bucket reporting for audits."

2) Throughput guarantees / measurement:
   - Guarantee: Customer is entitled to a minimum of (Committed DCUs * DCU_throughput) tokens/sec at the Tenant level measured as the 5-minute moving average at p95.
   - Auditability: Redwood will provide time-series metrics and raw sampling for third-party audits under NDA.

3) SLA & Service credits
   - Definitions: Scheduled Maintenance, Unscheduled Downtime, and Degraded Performance are defined in the attached SLA section.
   - Remedy: Service credits are tiered by severity; maximum monthly credit capped at 15% of the monthly Dedicated fee under standard 12-month commits. For 24-month commits or >1.5x committed DCU volume, Redwood will increase the cap to 20%. Credits are applied to the next invoice.

4) Burst & overage
   - Burst: Per-DCU 20% free burst up to the stated limits.
   - Overage billing: Measured hourly based on minutes over the burst allowance at 1.5x standard DCU rate.

Next steps: if that language looks reasonable we'll incorporate it into the SOW and flag the redlines to Marissa for a final pass. Would HealthGrid be open to the 24-month accelerated credit cap in exchange for a 10% deeper commit discount at the >500 DCU tier?

Happy to hop on a short call to walk procurement/legal through the terms.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0112

From: Elena Santos <elena.santos@healthgrid.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: Daniel Kim <daniel.kim@healthgrid.com>, procurement@healthgrid.com
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 15:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU commitment — capacity unit definition & SLA redlines

Jonas — appreciate the clear write-up and the mapping table. A few follow-ups from Legal and Finance after review of the draft: 

1) DCU baseline reference to a specific GPU model is OK, but we need an explicit fallback if Redwood needs to change hardware during the term (for supply/upgrade reasons). Proposed contract language: "Redwood may change underlying GPU hardware but must maintain parity within +/- 10% of the published DCU throughput and provide a 30-day remediation test window if Customer objects."

2) Measurement: we prefer p95 latency (end-to-end request latency at the tenant level) as the SLA metric rather than tokens/sec. Tokens/sec is useful to size pools but latency is what impacts our service and is what our SLAs to our customers measure. Can Redwood commit to measuring both and use p95 latency as the primary remedy trigger?

3) Service credit cap: Thanks for the 15% starting point. Finance requests an explicit escalation path: if Redwood misses the throughput/latency guarantees for 3 consecutive months, HealthGrid wants the ability to apply a remedial discount equal to up to 50% of the monthly Dedicated fee and an exit right with 60 days' notice (limited to extraordinary failure). We understand this is material — happy to discuss a middle ground.

4) Audit window: for metrics and audit logs, we need a 180-day retention copy accessible for download.

Please propose language that balances remediation visibility with Redwood's operational risk. If you can produce a redline that captures both the DCU fallback, p95 primary metric, and an escalation path (with caps) we'll route to CFO and Legal.

Thanks,
Elena

From: jonas.weber@redwood.ai <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Santos <elena.santos@healthgrid.com>
Cc: karchik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, procurement@healthgrid.com
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU commitment — capacity unit definition & SLA redlines

Elena — thanks, that feedback is very constructive. I discussed with Marissa (legal) and Karthik (pricing) over the weekend and we've prepared the following compromise proposal we think is straightforward and fair: 

1) Hardware changes: Redwood will publish any intended hardware changes 60 days in advance. New hardware must meet parity of +/- 12% of published DCU throughput. If HealthGrid disputes parity, Hayden (Redwood SRE) will run a 14-day performance test on a representative Tenant slice. If parity fails, Redwood will either revert to previous hardware for HealthGrid's pool or provide a pro-rated credit for the performance delta for up to 90 days while remediation is completed.

2) SLA metric & measurement: Redwood will measure both metrics. Primary trigger for credits will be p95 end-to-end latency at the Tenant level (as requested). Tokens/sec will be included as a secondary measurement for sizing/forecasting and to determine root cause of degradations. All metrics available through Redwood Console; we will provide a 180-day export on request for audits (satisfies your retention ask).

3) Escalation & credit cap: Standard monthly service credit cap remains 20% of Monthly Dedicated fees for customers with 24-month commits >= 500 DCUs. For customers on 12-month commits or <500 DCUs, cap remains 15%. Regarding the 50% remedial discount + exit right for 3 consecutive months of misses: we cannot accept an unrestricted 50% reduction or immediate exit — that would materially impair our ability to serve. Instead we propose a stepped remediation: 
   - 1st month miss: service credits as per SLA (calculated against p95 and applied to next invoice).
   - 2nd consecutive month miss: additional operational remediation credit equal to 25% of Monthly Dedicated fee and mandatory joint SRE review with HealthGrid.
   - 3rd consecutive month miss: remediation credit up to 40% of Monthly Dedicated fee plus right for HealthGrid to terminate the Dedicated SOW with 60 days' notice (termination right limited to performance breaches confirmed by independent audit and subject to cure periods).

This preserves an escalation path while capping Redwood's exposure. If HealthGrid needs an unconditional 50% cap and immediate exit, we can consider that only with a materially higher price (we can provide a delta).

4) Burst/overage & billing: we'll include explicit hourly measurement, and provide a billing simulator in the proposal so Finance can model worst-case and typical cases.

Next steps: I'll attach an updated SOW redline incorporating the above and highlight the specific legal clauses for quick review. If HealthGrid is willing to accept the stepped remediation model, Karthik will add a 10% commit discount at the 24-month 500+ DCU tier and we'll schedule DocuSign once Procurement confirms final SOW language.

Would you be available Wednesday 14 Jul at 10am PT for a 30-minute finalize-and-next-steps call?

Thanks again — appreciate the collaborative negotiation.

Best,
Jonas
